title: Support Engineer
description: Support Engineer Edinburgh Wordsmith Wordsmith is building the legal operating system for in-house teams, and we are growing fast. We believe in-house legal is becoming one of the most important functions in the AI era. Every business is moving faster, but legal work is still too often scattered across inboxes, chats, documents and disconnected systems. Wordsmith brings that work into one system. Requests come in from across the business, AI agents handle the routine, lawyers stay in control where judgement matters, and every step is captured as work happens. We are built for in-house legal, not law firms. Our goal is to help legal teams move faster, reduce unnecessary external counsel spend and become a function the business can run with. More than 500 companies, including Financial Times, Safelite, Trip.com , Canva, Starling and Sage, use Wordsmith. Backed by over $100M from Index Ventures, General Catalyst, Highland Europe and others, we are building one of the defining companies in legal AI. The role We’re hiring a Support Engineer to provide fast, thoughtful and technically rigorous help to Wordsmith customers. You’ll own technical questions and incidents from first response through to resolution. You’ll understand what the customer is trying to achieve, reproduce reported behaviour, investigate the underlying cause and explain the outcome clearly. This is more than scripted customer support. You’ll be expected to investigate application behaviour at a technical level, including reading logs and tracing issues through the product and its codebase. Where appropriate to your experience, you may also propose and submit code fixes through our normal engineering review and release process. Wordsmith supports customers globally through a follow-the-sun model. You’ll work the standard hours for your region and hand over unresolved issues clearly to colleagues in other regions. There is no routine expectation that you work another region’s hours. What you’ll do Own technical support requests — triage, investigate and resolve customer questions and incidents from first response to confirmed resolution. Diagnose problems thoroughly — gather the right context, reproduce reported behaviour, inspect logs and data, and trace issues through the product and codebase. Resolve technical issues — correct configuration or usage problems directly and collaborate with Engineering when a product or infrastructure change is required. Contribute code fixes where appropriate — depending on your experience, propose and submit well-tested fixes through the standard engineering review and deployment process. Communicate clearly — give customers timely and accurate updates, explain technical issues without unnecessary jargon and set honest expectations. Manage escalations — bring in Engineering, Product or other specialists when needed while retaining ownership of the case and its communication. Support global handovers — document investigation, impact, current status and next actions so colleagues in another region can continue work without losing momentum. Protect service quality — recognise high-impact incidents quickly, follow the appropriate escalation process and contribute to incident reviews. Build customer knowledge — create and maintain troubleshooting guides, known-issue documentation and help-centre content. Reduce repeat problems — identify patterns in support demand and recommend improvements to the product, documentation, tooling and customer experience. Improve support operations — help develop service levels, escalation paths, reporting and technical-support processes as the function scales. What we’re looking for Experience in technical support, product support, software engineering, solutions engineering or another customer-facing technical role. Strong diagnostic ability — you can work methodically from symptoms to root cause rather than relying on guesswork. A working understanding of modern web applications, APIs, authentication, integrations and common browser or network issues. Experience using diagnostic information such as application logs, monitoring tools, browser developer tools and database queries. Enough familiarity with software code to navigate a codebase, follow application logic and use it to investigate reported behaviour. Clear customer communication — you can remain calm under pressure, set expectations honestly and explain complex issues at the right level of detail. title: Global Head of Commercial Negotiations
description: Help us use technology to make a big green dent in the universe! Kraken powers some of the most innovative global developments in energy. We create the technology that redefines utilities and unlocks a new energy system of the future. By optimising renewable generation, building a more intelligent grid, and empowering utilities to deliver an exceptional customer experience, our operating system is transforming the industry worldwide. It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone. 🏡 Where you'll fit in You'll own strategic technology negotiations end to end. That covers tier-1 SaaS, outsourcing, and core billing platform deals for regulated utilities and energy retailers. You'll report to the Chief Commercial Officer and carry board-level accountability for deals above $100m. You'll lead a cross-functional deal team and make sure every seat is filled by the right person: Executive sponsor and deal owner: holds the mandate and budget, and breaks deadlocks fast. Lead negotiator: runs the table, controls pacing and concessions, and stays separate from the delivery owner. This is the seat you'll usually hold. Commercial and pricing lead: builds the should-cost model and covers pricing structures, benchmarking, and total cost of ownership (TCO). Legal and contracts counsel: covers liability caps, intellectual property (IP) ownership, indemnities, termination, data protection, and step-in rights. Technical and solution architect: tests feasibility, scope, service levels (SLAs), and integration and security claims. Operations and service owner: brings realistic requirements, transition plans, and governance from the business. Finance and procurement: covers payment terms, currency and indexation, and audit and benchmarking rights. Risk, security, and compliance: handles regulatory, data residency, and resilience requirements. 🚀 What you'll own Lead negotiation of multi-year technology and outsourcing agreements worth $250m to $1bn+ in total contract value, from selection through signature. Set the commercial playbook: pricing structures, walk-away positions, a concession log, and fallback positions on liability, service levels, and exit. Agree one position before you sit down. Rank priorities as must-have, trade, or give, and define your walk-away point (your best alternative to a negotiated agreement, or BATNA). Structure deals that fit the risk: fixed price, time and materials, outcome-based, and gain-share, with volume bands, rate cards, indexation, and price-down glide paths. Decide which risks to transfer, share, or keep, and put a price on each one. Negotiate core billing and Customer Information System (CIS) replacements, including migration plans, regulatory change, service levels, and exit terms. Define scope precisely: baseline, assumptions, dependencies, and exclusions. Most disputes start here, so you'll settle them before signature. Plan the exit from day one: lock-in, data portability, step-in rights, and termination assistance. Build competitive tension, keep alternatives alive, and manage timing, such as a vendor's quarter-end. Bring Delivery and Operations into the deal early, so the contract works in practice. Lock in key-personnel clauses, so the vendor's A-team doesn't sell while the B-team delivers. Set up governance, benchmarking, and audit rights that keep working after signature, and track change requests, renewals, and exit costs alongside the headline price. Recruit and grow the team: energy-billing experts, a migration lead, SaaS counsel, and regulatory specialists, with a clear capability model and a RACI (who's responsible, accountable, consulted, and informed). Coach executive sponsors on leverage and timing, and run negotiation war-gaming before the big moments. Step in early when a deal or migration drifts, and reset milestones, scope, and commercials to get it back on track. 🧠 What you'll bring to the party Experience Ideally 20+ years negotiating multi-year technology and outsourcing agreements for regulated utilities or energy retailers. A track record on 15+ transactions of $250m to $1bn+ total contract value, including core billing or CIS replacement, cloud migration, or managed services. Energy domain knowledge: meter-to-cash, tariffs, market codes, and regulatory billing obligations. The credibility to work with boards, CFOs, and regulators, and to say no when a deal doesn't add up. Capabilities Commercial acumen. You understand vendor economics and margin levers, and you know where suppliers make their money (change requests and renewals, for example). Deal structuring. You choose between fixed price, time and materials, outcome-based, and gain-share, and you set volume bands and price-down paths that hold up over 3 to 7 years. Risk allocation judgment. You know which risks to transfer, share, or keep, and you can price them. Technical depth. You can challenge a vendor's assumptions on scope, effort, and architecture. Scope and requirements clarity. You define what's in, what's out, and what has to be true for the price to hold. Exit and transition planning. You cover lock-in, data portability, step-in, and termination assistance from the start. Commercial modeling. You build multi-year margin, cash flow, cost-to-serve, and should-cost models. How you work You bring one voice to the table. No side deals, and every concession goes in the log. You build leverage with a competitive process, and you keep your composure when a vendor pushes a deadline or a "sign now for a discount" offer. You push hard on terms and protect the long-term partnership, because we'll live with the deal for years. You work well across cultures and time zones, including with vendors based in other markets. You bring legal, commercial, and technical colleagues into one room instead of letting them negotiate in silos. ⭐ Bonus points Time spent on the supplier side, so you know how vendor economics and margin levers work from the inside. A legal or contracts background. Negotiation or value-selling certifications, such as Harvard PON. Working knowledge of Ofgem licence conditions, the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), and operational resilience rules such as the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA). A degree in business, engineering, law, or a related field. Are you ready for a career with us? We want to ensure you have the right tools and environment to unleash your potential. title: Finance Forecasting Modeller
description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong><em>🚀 We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone.</em></strong></p> <p>We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.</p> <p>After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. As well as <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/personal">personal</a> and <a href="https://monzo.com/business-banking">business</a> bank accounts, we offer <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/joint-account">joint accounts</a>, <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/16-17">accounts for 16-17 year olds</a>, a <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/under-16s">free kids account</a> and <a href="https://monzo.com/flex">credit cards</a> in the UK, with more exciting things to come beyond. Our UK customers can also <a href="https://monzo.com/savings">save</a>, <a href="https://monzo.com/investments">invest </a>and <a href="https://monzo.com/pensions">combine their pensions</a> with us. </p> <p>With our hot coral cards and get-paid-early feature, combined with financial education on social media and our award winning customer service, we have a long history of creating magical moments for our customers!</p> <p>We’re not about selling products - we want to solve problems and change lives through Monzo ❤️</p> <hr> <p> </p></div><p>📍 London (UK)  | 💰 £79,000 to £106,800 + Incentive Awards tied to your performance +<a href="https://monzo.com/careers#benefits"> Benefits</a></p> <p> </p> <p><strong>Our Capital, Impairments & Forecasting Team ⭐</strong></p> <p>Our Capital, Impairments & Forecasting team (CIF) sits at the intersection of our Borrowing and Finance collectives, responsible for developing, executing and managing the models used to calculate IFRS 9 ECL, and credit risk capital through the annual ICAAP. We work alongside our first line credit teams who design the products, decide who to lend to, set underwriting policy, identify customers who need help, manage the portfolio and report and measure credit risk.</p> <p>Within CIF, we are scaling up our Forecasting modelling and execution team to support the enhancement of modelling standards across Finance. The role holder will have the opportunity to lead a ‘consultancy style’ centre of excellence providing thought leadership on the methodological design and regulatory compliance assessment on all Financial forecasting models that feed the banks’ budgeting and stress-testing activities. This will expand to hands-on delivery of model developments, where appropriate. </p> <p>Strong data and analytical skills are a must, as is experience in financial modelling and coding (Python and SQL preferred). Experience working in regulatory stress testing exercises (such as ICAAP or EBA Stress-testing) is highly desirable but not essential. </p> <p>We rely heavily on the following tools and technologies (note we do not expect applicants to have prior experience of all them):</p> <ul> <li><a href="https://cloud.google.com/">Google Cloud Platform</a> for all of our analytics infrastructure</li> <li><a href="https://www.getdbt.com/">dbt</a> and<a href="https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/"><strong> </strong>BigQuery SQL</a> for our data modelling and warehousing</li> <li>Python for data science and predictive modelling and data visualisation (via streamlit)</li> <li>Anaplan for model implementation</li> <li>Github for version control</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>🔑 You’ll play a key role by...</strong></p> <ul> <li>Assisting with continuous improvement of forecasting models via individual delivery or through others</li> <li>Development of best practices for financial modelling across Monzo</li> <li>Presenting forecast model results to senior management</li> <li>Close collaboration with portfolio strategy, model validation, finance and external audit teams</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>🤩 We’d love to hear from you if…</strong></p> <ul> <li>You have a background in financial forecast modelling or execution</li> <li>You have strong analytical skills and a track record of using these to deliver technical projects</li> <li>You have a solid technical toolkit. SQL and Python are our desired coding languages but experience in SAS/R will be considered. A data visualisation tool (such as Streamlit or Looker) is a plus</li> <li>You can convey problems and solutions using clear and simple language, both written and verbal (see <a href="https://monzo.com/tone-of-voice/">Monzo’s tone of voice</a> guide). This is particularly important for communicating complex issues and priorities to non-experts</li> <li>You're impact driven and eager to have a real positive impact on the company, our products, our users and your team-mates</li> <li>You have a self-starter mindset<em>;</em> you proactively identify issues and opportunities and tackle them without being told to do so</li> <li>You're a team player<em> </em>whom your colleagues can rely on</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>🌈 The application journey has 4 key steps</strong></p> <ol> <li>Initial call with a member of the Forecasting team</li> <li>Technical modelling interview </li> <li>Values and collaboration behavioural interview</li> <li>A live case study problem solving interview</li> </ol> <p>Our average process takes around 3-4 weeks but we will always work around your availability.</p> <p> </p> <p><strong>🙌 What’s in it for you</strong></p> <p>💰 £79,000 to £106,800 + <a href="https://monzo.com/careers/">benefits</a>  </p> <p>📍 London (one day a week)</p> <p>✈️ We can help you relocate to the UK</p> <p>✅ We can sponsor visas</p> <p>⏰ We offer flexible working hours and trust you to work enough hours to do your job well, at times that suit you and your team.</p> <p>📚Learning budget of £1,000 a year for books, training courses and conferences</p> <p>➕And much more, see our full list of benefits <a href="https://monzo.com/careers/">here</a></p> <p> </p> <p><span class="notion-enable-hover" data-token-index="0">#LI-JH1</span></p><div class="content-conclusion"><hr> <p><strong>Equal opportunities for everyone</strong></p> <p>Diversity and inclusion are a priority for us and we’re making sure we have lots of support for all of our people to grow at Monzo. At Monzo, we’re embracing diversity by fostering an inclusive environment for all people to do the best work of their lives with us. This is integral to our mission of making money work for everyone. You can read more in our <a href="https://monzo.com/blog/diversity-and-inclusion">blog</a>, 2026 <a href="https://monzo.com/blog/our-2026-diversity-and-inclusion-report" target="_blank">Diversity and Inclusion Report</a> and 2025 <a href="https://monzo.com/blog/gender-pay-gap-report-2025">Gender Pay Gap Report.</a></p> <p>We’re an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to age, ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, or veteran, neurodiversity or disability status.</p> <p>If you have a preferred name, please use it to apply. We don't need full or birth names at application stage 😊</p></div>

title: Special Projects Lead - Category Expansion
description: Can you help us fix the world's most broken supply chain? The fashion industry produces over 100 billion garments a year. 60% end up in landfill, not because people don't want these clothes, but because the supply chain for getting secondhand fashion from donation to resale is completely offline, manual and broken. Fleek is fixing this. Our mission is to make secondhand the first choice. We're building the infrastructure powering the global secondhand clothing trade, through a B2B marketplace and the AI systems digitising the supply chain behind it. Through Fleek, vintage stores, online resellers and retail buyers source graded secondhand inventory directly from wholesalers and rag houses across multiple countries. Our key enabler is FleekSort, an AI model fine-tuned on secondhand fashion that can grade, price and categorise items with just a photo. Turning what has historically been an opaque and manual trade into a structured, searchable and tradable global inventory layer. Since 2022, we've saved 9 million items from landfill while tripling in size year-on-year. We're backed by some of the world's best investors, including a16z, Y Combinator and HV Capital, alongside world-class angels who helped build Depop, Shopify, and Postmates. Today, we serve thousands of resellers and retailers across the UK, Europe and the US. With the secondhand fashion market projected to reach $350B by 2027, Fleek is building the AI-native operational and financial backbone for secondhand commerce globally. We're looking for people who want to build something that matters and move fast doing it. Sounds good? Keep reading. About the Role We're hiring a Special Projects Lead to take Fleek's new category bets from thesis to proven economics. Each is a new business line that could add £5M+ in GMV, opening a new supply category or a new sourcing geography for the marketplace. Here's what makes these bets unusually winnable. Fleek already owns the demand. Most of the live bets sell to buyers who transact on Fleek today, so they're a supply-first test rather than a two-sided cold start. Your job on a new bet is to find and onboard the supply, sell it into demand that already exists and read the economics fast. Every bet runs through the same gates. If a bet misses its gates, you kill it with evidence and move to the next one. If it works and you're running it well, you don't have to hand it off. You scale into owning the category, with supply, acquisition and ops building out under you. Think of this seat as a venture builder inside Fleek. One thing this is not. We're not building a sales team or a sales culture, and this is not an AE or account manager role with a new title. You'll work directly with the founders and our commercial lead, close to the centre of the company. What You'll Do Run bets through the gates: take each bet from market research to first suppliers to first GMV to a feasible-or-not call, with win metrics and kill metrics defined before you start. Go where the supply is: get on planes. You'll visit suppliers, graders and rag houses in the markets your bets open up, because this trade is built face to face and the best stock never gets listed anywhere. Sell supply into live demand: onboard brands, brokers, graders and wholesalers, then get Fleek's existing buyers transacting on the new inventory. The sell is fast, informal and relationship-led, over WhatsApp and Instagram as often as in a boardroom. Make the kill calls: hold a clear view of unit economics and the competitive landscape on every bet. Double down or cut on evidence, not attachment. Be the ops function, for now: work out importer-of-record structures, duties, freight cost and last mile for each new flow. Ride the AI infrastructure: our acquisition team has spent months building the agentic outreach and enrichment engine. You'll plug your bets into it and extend it, rather than building from a blank page or adding headcount. Learn the actual trade: how stock is graded, routed and priced across markets, and who's sitting on good inventory that nobody has approached. You'll get deep in it fast. What You Bring Zero-to-one is your natural habitat. You've built something from nothing as a founder, an early employee or the person who started a new line inside an existing company. You've operated without a playbook and you didn't wait for one. Operator and commercial in one person. You build the machine and you carry the number. You're not pure strategy and you're not pure sales, and you're comfortable being measured on GMV within your first quarter. AI fluency. You work with agents and automations daily and you'd rather build a workflow than repeat a task. Strong signals on top of that: An instinct for physical goods. You understand inventory, margins and trading relationships, or you've worked around fashion, resale or marketplaces. Deals you structured yourself, at any size, that didn't exist before you wrote them. Exposure to cross-border trade, logistics or supply chain operations. Nice to Have Direct experience in resale, surplus or secondary-market inventory Experience launching a new market, geography or product line from scratch Established networks in international sourcing markets What You'll Get Generous equity: being on Fleek means you'll own a part of it Comprehensive healthcare coverage A collaborative team in a lovely office in the heart of East London Access to founders. We're a small team and they're heavily involved (and good fun!) Exclusive employee discounts to buy on Fleek Access to borrow any item from our collection of vintage and reworks in the office A disproportionate level of responsibility and the opportunity to drive massive impact How We Work Fleek is an in-office company. We're based at Commercial Street, E1 (Liverpool Street / Aldgate East). We operate a fully in-person culture at our office in Shoreditch, with trust-based flexibility. We hire adults and trust them to perform. The Practicalities Location: London HQ, Commercial Street, E1 (Liverpool Street / Aldgate East) Stage: Post-Series B, hyper-growth Team: 200 across three geographies Culture: High ownership, non-hierarchical, fast-moving. Founder-led with strong opinions loosely held. Our Values Five values shape how we work at Fleek: Dream Big and Disrupt Yourself: Push the most ambitious version of what you're building. Step out of your comfort zone. Nothing is out of reach. Absolute Ownership: The buck stops with you. Drive initiatives to completion. Experiment, learn, persevere. The job isn't done until the job is done. Curiosity Leads the Way: Don't accept anything at face value. Ask questions you don't know the answer to. That's how you innovate. Talk to the Customer: Deeply understand their challenges, motivations, and ambitions. Every decision starts with the customer at the centre. Embrace Diversity: A global team building for a global supply chain. Bring your authentic self and embrace the diversity of everyone you encounter. title: Talent Director
description: About OLIX AI is growing faster than any technology in history and the explosion in demand has created a massive infrastructure gap; we can no longer build chips or power stations fast enough to keep up. The OLIX Decode Accelerator 1 (DX-1) is the first accelerator architected specifically for decode. Rack-scale co-design of logic, data movement, packaging, optics and interconnect enables a step change in system level performance. The Role The Talent Director owns how OLIX finds, wins and hires the people who will build it. You will take a talent function built for around 200 people and make it one that carries us confidently to 1,000, across London, Bristol, Austin, San Francisco and Toronto, without lowering the bar on a single hire. This is a hands on leadership role. You will personally lead our most senior and executive searches, and close people who are not looking. Many of the people we need exist in pools of a few dozen worldwide: III-V device engineers, advanced packaging architects, optical interconnect specialists, AI software engineers, silicon leaders who have taken a chip to production. Hiring them is a precision problem, not a volume one. You will build a team of recruiters as sharp as the engineers they hire, and set an AI strategy for recruiting that changes how we decide, not just how fast we work. The best argument wins here, and we expect you to make it, welcome challenges to it, and change your mind when the evidence says so. Responsibilities Build and scale the talent function from around 200 to 1,000 people: org design, hiring, priorities and operating rhythm, in place before the headcount arrives Lead senior and executive searches directly, including the hires that signal the calibre of people joining OLIX Attract, hire and develop top Recruiters and Sourcers, and hold them to the same bar as our engineers Own the hiring bar: what great looks like for each role family, and how consistently every interviewer applies it Build the playbook for extremely scarce talent: mapping the market, building relationships early, and closing passive candidates Set OLIX's AI strategy for recruiting, deciding where AI improves our judgement and where people need to stay in the loop Own hiring systems, data and metrics, and partner with the exec team on workforce planning, including saying when a plan is not hireable as written Build OLIX's talent brand so the best people in photonics, silicon and AI know who we are Skills & Experience Has built and led a talent function through hyper-growth, from a few hundred people toward 1,000 or beyond, while keeping quality high. description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong><em>🚀 We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone.</em></strong></p> <p>We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.</p> <p>After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. You'll become the subject matter expert for intercompany processes, helping ensure transactions between entities are accurate, well controlled and completed on time.</p> <p>This role combines financial planning activities with project-based work, giving you exposure to forecasting, reporting, governance, process improvement and stakeholder management across Finance and the wider business.</p> <p>You'll work closely with Finance Business Partners, Financial Control, Group FP&A and business stakeholders, helping provide high quality financial information that supports good decision making.</p> <p><strong>🔑 You’ll play a key role by…</strong></p> <ul> <li>Producing monthly forecasts, variance analysis and reporting for Monzo's subsidiary entities, ensuring forecasts remain accurate and well understood.</li> <li>Owning the administration and coordination of the intercompany charging process, ensuring transactions are processed accurately, approved correctly and completed to timetable.</li> <li>Preparing financial reporting for strategic projects, monitoring spend against approved budgets and highlighting financial risks, opportunities and delivery performance.</li> <li>Supporting month end activities by preparing journals, reconciliations, accruals and reporting schedules in partnership with Financial Control.</li> <li>Investigating financial variances and explaining the commercial drivers behind changes in spend, forecasting assumptions and project performance.</li> <li>Working with stakeholders across Finance and the business to gather forecast inputs, resolve data issues and improve the quality of financial information.</li> <li>Maintaining financial models, reporting templates and process documentation to improve consistency, governance and operational efficiency.</li> <li>Supporting investment business cases by gathering financial information, validating assumptions and preparing analysis for decision making.</li> <li>Identifying opportunities to automate manual activities and improve finance processes through better use of systems and data.</li> <li>Helping deliver finance transformation initiatives by supporting testing, implementation and continuous improvement projects.</li> </ul> <p><strong>🤩 We’d love to hear from you if…</strong></p> <ul> <li>Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret financial data and identify meaningful insights.</li> <li>Excellent attention to detail, producing accurate work even when managing multiple priorities.</li> <li>Confidence working with large datasets and using data to solve business problems.</li> <li>Strong organisation and planning skills, delivering work to agreed deadlines.</li> <li>Clear written and verbal communication skills, able to explain financial information simply.</li> <li>A collaborative approach, building positive relationships with colleagues across Finance and the wider business.</li> <li>Curiosity and a continuous improvement mindset, always looking for better ways of working.</li> <li>Personal accountability, taking ownership of work and following through on commitments.</li> <li>Automation and technology mindset with the ability to identify manual processes, define automation opportunities and partner with technical teams to implement scalable solutions.</li> <li>Analytical and problem solving capability with the ability to use data and insight to identify root causes, evaluate options and implement practical, value adding solutions.</li> <li>Continuous improvement mindset with a passion for challenging the status quo, embedding best practice and creating a culture of operational excellence and learning.</li> </ul> <p><strong>🙌What’s in it for you</strong></p> <p>💰 £45,500 - £57,500 + Incentive Awards tied to performance. </p> <p>📍 This role is based in our London office, with a hybrid working environment with flexible working from home arrangements and some in-person attendance. We're open to distributed working within the UK (with the expectation of occasional work from our London office for key meetings).</p> <p>⏰ We offer flexible working hours and trust you to work enough hours to do your job well, and at times that suit you and your team. </p> <p>📚 £1,000 learning budget each year to use on books, training courses and conferences.</p> <p>🏡 We will set you up to work from home; all employees are given Macbooks and for fully remote workers we will provide extra support for your work-from-home setup. </p> <p>➕ Plus lots more! <a href="https://monzo.com/careers/">Read our full list of benefits<br><br></a></p> <p><strong>🌈</strong><strong> The application journey has 3 key steps:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Recruiter Screening Call </li> <li>Role Specific Interview </li> <li>Final Interview with the Hiring Manager </li> </ul> <p>Our average process takes around 3-4 weeks but we will always work around your availability. </p> <p>We’ll only close this role once we have enough applications for the next stage. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to age, ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, or veteran, neurodiversity or disability status.</p> <p>If you have a preferred name, please use it to apply. We don't need full or birth names at application stage 😊</p></div>

title: Director Solutions Platform, UK
description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong>About WPP Media</strong></p> <p>WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. Connected through WPP Open and powered by Open Intelligence, clients see exactly where, how, and why their media investment is working.</p> <p>For more information, visit <a href="wppmedia.com">wppmedia.com</a>.</p></div><h3><strong>Role Purpose</strong></h3> <p>The Platform Operations Director is responsible for ensuring that solutions developed and released for the Solutions team are operationally ready, properly tested, clearly documented, effectively released, and provide support once live.</p> <p>The role acts as the bridge between delivery, business readiness and BAU operations. It supports the transition of work from project delivery into stable operational use, ensuring that users, stakeholders and support teams understand what has changed, how to use it, how to raise issues, and how ongoing support will be managed with appropriate priority, impact and SLAs</p> <p>This role is particularly important as Solutions Integration moves from a more reactive service model into a structured product and agile delivery function. The Platform Operations Director owns QA, release management, documentation, stakeholder communication, support processes, training, adoption and post-release improvement including BAU bugs and triage.</p> <p>The role works closely with Product Owners, Scrum Master, Engineering, Data, Reporting, QA, Platform Operations, and business stakeholders to make sure delivery does not stop at “built”, but continues through testing, launch, adoption, support and measurable operational value.</p> <h2><strong>Senior / Specialist-Level Expectations</strong></h2> <p>As a Director within the team, this role is expected to help define and improve the operating standards around BAU management, QA coordination, release readiness, business readiness and service transition. Manage and proactively manage risk, resolution SLAs and ensure we are adhering to platform operational best practices.</p> <p>The Platform Operations Director should be able to identify operational risks early, challenge whether a solution is genuinely ready for release, and recommend practical improvements to processes, documentation, testing, support models and stakeholder communications.</p> <p>For smaller initiatives, the role should be able to advise Product Owners and delivery teams on the appropriate level of QA, training, release planning, handover and BAU support required. For larger or more complex initiatives, the role should escalate risks, dependencies or readiness gaps to the Product Manager Lead, Scrum Master, Lead Engineer / Solutions Architect or relevant leadership stakeholders.</p> <h1><strong>Key Responsibilities</strong></h1> <h2><strong>1. BAU Operations Management</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Own and coordinate BAU operational processes for assigned platforms, tools, reports, workflows and solutions across all Media solutions.</li> <li>Monitor recurring issues, support trends, operational risks and user pain points.</li> <li>Triage and prioritise BAU requests, incidents, defects and enhancement requests.</li> <li>Ensure BAU work is captured through the agreed intake and backlog process rather than unmanaged emails, verbal requests or fragmented ticket routes.</li> <li>Work with Product Owners and the Scrum Master to distinguish between BAU support, defects, enhancements and new product requirements.</li> <li>Maintain visibility of BAU demand and help identify where recurring issues should become product improvements or engineering fixes.</li> <li>Support continuous improvement of support processes, documentation and operational workflows.</li> </ul> <p>This links directly to the team’s wider shift away from fragmented request routes and towards clearer delivery rhythms, structured backlogs and improved operational process discipline. The existing documentation notes the need for clearer team rhythms, sprint cadences, retrospectives and mentoring as part of the transition plan .</p> <h2><strong>2. QA Coordination and Testing Readiness</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Coordinate QA activity across delivery workstreams, ensuring testing requirements are understood before development begins.</li> <li>Work with Product Owners to ensure acceptance criteria, test scenarios and success measures are clearly defined.</li> <li>Support test planning across functional testing, regression testing, data validation, reporting checks and user acceptance testing.</li> <li>Ensure defects are logged, prioritised, tracked and resolved through the agreed delivery process.</li> <li>Work with engineers, analysts and business users to validate that solutions meet functional, operational and reporting requirements.</li> <li>Support the creation of reusable QA checklists, test scripts and validation templates.</li> <li>Ensure solutions are not released without appropriate testing evidence and business sign-off.</li> </ul> <p>This is consistent with the Product Owner responsibilities already defined around testing requirements, success criteria, UAT coordination, business validation, release readiness and operational handover . The Platform Operations Specialist would support and operationalise those activities.</p> <h2><strong>3. Business Readiness and Adoption</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Ensure business users and operational teams are ready to adopt new or changed solutions.</li> <li>Coordinate training, guidance, demos, FAQs, release notes and user communications.</li> <li>Work with Product Owners to identify impacted teams, users, processes and workflows.</li> <li>Confirm that business teams understand what is changing, why it is changing, when it is happening and what action is required.</li> <li>Support stakeholder communications before, during and after release.</li> <li>Gather early feedback from users and ensure issues are captured and prioritised appropriately.</li> <li>Help ensure delivered solutions are embedded into day-to-day operations, rather than remaining underused or misunderstood.</li> </ul> <p>The handover documentation highlights the importance of clear communication with users, proper release notes, demonstrations and adoption support for new features and solutions . This role should own the operational discipline around making that happen consistently.</p> <h2><strong>4. Release Readiness and Service Transition</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Own or coordinate release readiness checklists for assigned solutions.</li> <li>Ensure each release has appropriate testing evidence, documentation, support ownership, training material and stakeholder communication.</li> <li>Coordinate operational handover from delivery teams into BAU support.</li> <li>Confirm that runbooks, troubleshooting guides, known issues and escalation routes are in place.</li> <li>Work with engineering and data teams to ensure monitoring, alerting or manual checks are defined where required.</li> <li>Support go-live planning, release scheduling and post-release hypercare.</li> <li>Track post-release issues and ensure learnings are fed back into future delivery cycles.</li> </ul> <p>This role should become the person asking:</p> <p>“Are we actually ready to put this live, support it, explain it, and measure whether it worked?”</p> <h2><strong>5. Documentation and Knowledge Management</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Maintain clear operational documentation for platforms, reports, tools, processes and workflows.</li> <li>Support the creation of user guides, SOPs, runbooks, release notes, FAQs and support documentation.</li> <li>Ensure documentation is stored in the agreed location and kept up to date.</li> <li>Work with Product Owners, engineers and analysts to document key dependencies, business rules, known limitations and support processes.</li> <li>Help reduce reliance on individual knowledge by making processes and system behaviour transparent.</li> <li>Support onboarding of new team members by maintaining accessible knowledge resources.</li> </ul> <p>This is important because the team is moving away from legacy ways of working and informal knowledge transfer into a more structured operating model.</p> <h2><strong>6. Platform and Process Governance</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Support the consistent use of agreed tools, workflows, ticketing processes and delivery governance.</li> <li>Help ensure work is captured, categorised and progressed through the correct routes.</li> <li>Maintain standards for BAU tickets, defects, release requests, support issues and operational change.</li> <li>Identify process gaps, duplicated effort or inconsistent ways of working.</li> <li>Recommend improvements to BAU processes, support models, QA standards and release governance.</li> <li>Support reporting on operational performance, support demand, defect trends and release readiness.</li> <li>Help ensure changes are controlled, documented and aligned to agreed team practices.</li> </ul> <p>This aligns with the documented need to improve proactive behaviour, structured product management, backlog grooming, stand-ups and retrospectives across the team .</p> <h2><strong>7. Stakeholder and Cross-Team Coordination</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Work closely with Product Owners, Engineering, Data, Reporting, QA, Scrum Master and business users.</li> <li>Coordinate with Activation, Operations, Channel Development, Commercial and other impacted teams where relevant.</li> <li>Ensure operational dependencies are understood and managed before release.</li> <li>Help stakeholders understand support routes, known issues, timelines and release impacts.</li> <li>Escalate operational risks, unresolved defects, readiness gaps or business adoption concerns.</li> <li>Support regular BAU and platform operations updates for leadership where required.</li> </ul> <p>The existing Product Owner documentation already describes the importance of coordination across engineering, data, reporting, platform, operations and business teams . Package complex media systems, technical mechanics, and multi-brand nuances into succinct, punchy, C-suite ready narratives that clearly articulate the "So What?".</li> <li>Visual & Verbal Clarity: Coach the planning cohort on visual layout, storyline momentum, and presentation delivery, setting a new benchmark for what an OpenConnect strategic deliverable looks and feels like.</li> </ul> </ol> <p><strong>Creative Agency Partnership & Ecosystem Integration</strong></p> <ol> <ul> <li>Inter-Agency Roster Leadership: Act as a strategic partner to creative and BT strategists across the BT Group roster. Build collaborative, high-trust working relationships that dismantle agency silos.</li> <li>Upstream Creative Collaboration: Where possible, engage early in the creative development cycle to influence ideation, ensuring creative platforms and media channel architectures complement, push, and amplify each other.</li> <li>Bridge the Creative/Media Divide: Serve as the connective tissue between creative ambition and media capability, co-developing unified campaign playbooks where media environments make the creative idea unmissable.</li> </ul> </ol> <p><strong>Multi-Brand & Enterprise Breadth (Consumer + B2B)</strong></p> <ol> <ul> <li>Consumer Portfolio Rigour: Maintain clear distinction, tone, and strategic guardrails across consumer brands, ensuring EE, BT, and Plusnet execute with distinct roles without internal friction or audience overlap.</li> <li>BT Business Acceleration: Partner with the enterprise leads to bring consumer-grade storytelling, behavioural insight, and dynamic comms planning into the B2B space (SMEs, Corporate, and Public Sector).</li> <li>Cross-Pollination: Identify shared learnings, testing frameworks, and effectiveness benchmarks across consumer campaigns and adapt them strategically for BT Business.</li> </ul> </ol> <p><strong>Team Upskilling</strong></p> <ol> <ul> <li>Arms around the team: Actively mentor, manage, and coach planners in the team, transforming them from reactive brief-takers into proactive strategic partners.</li> <li>Support on comms planning culture within the Open Connect team, bringing planners together in weekly council sessions, leading stretch sessions, training etc.</li> <li>Embed Best Practice: Institutionalise consistent comms planning toolkits, framing templates, and insight-mining methodologies across the entire account team; get them using the data at our fingertips, always looking beyond TGI! </li> <li>Instill Strategic Confidence: Build a team culture anchored in conviction, strategic bravery, and clear point-of-view, empowering planners to defend ideas and challenge client briefs with commercial intelligence.</li> </ul> </ol> <p><strong>Candidate Profile & Qualifications</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Senior Comms Planning clout:</strong> Experience in senior Comms Strategy/planning, Connections Planning, or Integrated Strategy roles within top-tier media or creative agencies.</li> <li><strong>Master Storyteller</strong>: Exceptional ability to distill messy, highly technical, and data-dense inputs into elegant, high-impact stories tailored for CMOs and Marketing Directors.</li> <li><strong>Insight Hunter</strong>: Demonstrated ability to find provocative, emotionally resonant human truths and cultural tensions that unlock fresh creative media solutions, not just reporting what the data says, but proving why it matters.</li> <li><strong>Creative Fluency</strong>: Experienced working alongside top creative agency strategy leads, with the diplomacy, creative vocabulary, and collaborative skill to shape work jointly.</li> <li><strong>B2C & B2B Versatility:</strong> Consumer comms experience combined with the intellectual curiosity and agility to tackle the complex, account-based nuances of BT Business.</li> <li><strong>Team Player: </strong>Natural mentor who loves developing planners, raising team morale through their positivity, enthusiasm and energy, to support building an environment of strategic excellence.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Life at WPP Media & Benefits</strong></p> <p>Our passion for shaping the next era of media is powered by our commitment to Be Extraordinary, investing in our employees to inspire transformational creativity. This integrated approach empowers you to craft media plans that are not only creative and impactful but also deeply informed, measurable, and strategically sound.</p> <p><strong><u>About the role</u></strong></p> <p>You will be expected to demonstrate experience and knowledge in -</p> <ul> <li>Knowing the tools and means to build and target audiences in addressable and non-addressable media to validate the media approach ensuring that the defined audience can be reached at the scale required</li> <li>Designing an approach that outlines how and where we will connect with defined audiences – especially hard to reach / low media engagement audiences – in media for brand and performance campaigns.</li> <li>Connecting the dots between the data we, the client, media owners and other internal teams hold to plan most effectively.</li> <li>Designing the connections ecosystem & plan, working closely and collaboratively with channel specialists and wider agency teams from a paid, owned and earned perspective</li> <li>Day to day management of campaigns and annual planning as a key liaison between clients and channel specialists</li> <li>Designing measurement & testing framework to inform as well as measure and optimise the campaigns when live</li> <li>Management of others to develop their skills</li> </ul> <p><strong>Skills and Experience</strong></p> <p>At WPP Media, we believe in the power of our culture and our people. description: Our Mission: Omnea is the agentic operating system for procurement. Over the next year, our engineering team will double in size, our enterprise customer base will grow from ~180 to 300+, and revenue will triple. As a Team Lead Manager, you’ll lead a small team of engineers. You’ll set its technical direction, line-manage and grow the people in it, and stay hands-on in the code. This is not a hands-off management role: our teams are small, and you’ll be one of the strongest engineers on yours. You’ll partner closely with a Product Manager and Product Designer to decide what to build, and you’ll be accountable for how well it’s built and how fast it ships. If you’re a strong Tech Lead who hasn’t managed people yet, we’d still love to hear from you. You can start as a Team Lead, with management handled by an Engineering Manager, and grow into the full role with our support. What Can You Expect As a Team Lead Manager? Lead and Manage a Small Team. Line-manage the engineers on your team, run 1:1s, give feedback, and help them take on bigger problems. Stay Deeply Technical. You’ll still build. Expect to spend a meaningful share of your time writing code, reviewing PRs, and unblocking the hardest technical problems. AI-Native Development. AI is core to how we build. Engineers use Claude, Code, and agentic workflows every day, and our product is built on AI agents that automate complex procurement workflows. You’ll set the bar for how your team uses them. Customers at the Center. Talk directly with customers to understand their problems, and make sure your team builds things that create real value for them. Own Technical Direction. Make the architecture and design calls for your team’s problem space, and own the trade-offs between speed, quality, and long-term maintainability. Work with Modern Technology. TypeScript across the stack, React, Postgres, and AWS serverless (Lambda, DynamoDB, EventBridge), managed through Pulumi and deployed via GitHub Actions. Datadog, Meticulous, and Incident.io round it out. Shape the Roadmap. Work with your PM and Designer on prioritisation, scoping, and sequencing so the team ships what matters most. Build the Team. Interview, hire, and onboard new engineers as we double in size. About You You’re a highly technical full-stack engineer. You’ve designed and shipped web apps end to end in TypeScript, ideally on AWS serverless, and you’re still one of the strongest engineers in the room. You’ve led engineers. You’ve been a Tech Lead, Team Lead, or TLM, owning delivery and technical direction for a team. You want to manage people, or grow into it. Ideally, you’ve line-managed engineers already. If not, you’re keen to learn. You still love to build. Leading hasn’t pulled you away from the code, and you want a role where you keep shipping. You raise the bar. You know what well-architected, reliable software looks like, and you help others get there through reviews, pairing, and clear feedback. You’re motivated by customer impact. You care about outcomes for customers, not just output, and you make good calls on what to build and what to cut. You’re a strong partner. You work well with product and design, push back when it matters, and bring people with you. You’re comfortable with ambiguity. You can take an unclear problem, shape it, and get a team moving on it. Nice-to-Haves You’ve led a team through fast growth, ideally at a scale-up where the team and product changed quickly. You’ve built B2B or enterprise SaaS, with complex workflows and demanding customers. You’ve performed exceptionally at something else, be it academics, sport, or work. Interview Process Before applying, we strongly encourage you to spend a few minutes in our R&D Candidate Hub. It covers our engineering culture, ways of working, interview process, tech environment, and what it’s like to build at Omnea. R&D Candidate Hub : https://omnea.notion.site/R-D-Candidate-Hub-2f688cce658780f1b942c81cd3a032d4 Note: our pair programming stage is in TypeScript OR Python and you’ll be assessed as if it’s your primary language. This is a full-stack, hands-on leadership role, so if you’re exclusively frontend, backend, or platform-focused, or no longer writing code, it likely isn’t the right fit. The process generally includes: Initial screening call with our Talent team (30 mins, remote) AI Product Eng Challenge , language-agnostic (1 hour, remote) Onsite interviews at our Victoria office (~3 hours) Engineering Culture interview with an Engineering Manager or Team Lead (45 mins) System Design interview with a Senior Engineer (60 mins) Engineering Leadership interview with our CTO (45 mins) Office tour (15 mins) We’re proud to support visa sponsorship for candidates who need it. At Omnea, we embrace diversity. To build a product that's loved by everyone, we're best served by a team with all sorts of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't quite match the full job spec! And regardless of your race, religion, colour, gender, or anything else! If you think you could be a good fit for Omnea, please reach out. A few things to note: We offer competitive geo-localised benefits, and you can check out our UK Benefits Package here and our US Benefits Package here . We work Tuesdays, Wednesdays & Thursdays in-person at our offices. At this early stage of our company life-cycle it's important to us that we get this together-time, and you can read more about why we believe this is a winning move here We're commercial, ambitious and we don't pretend otherwise! We're actively seeking folks looking to make the most of a career-defining opportunity, with the hunger to be part of building something really impressive . You can see our values here and our Omnea Future Founder's fund here ! We sometimes use AI note-takers to help us transcribe interview notes, so we can be more present in your interview. If you'd like to opt out of us using automatic transcribers, please note this in the free text field in your application, otherwise we'll take your application as confirmation that you're happy for us to use notetakers (whether added to video calls or in the background). We are proud to be recognised for both our culture and product, and we are just getting started. Join us as we grow! Our customers have cut a year or more from their certification timelines for new AI-enabled medical devices and shortened product-update cycles from months to weeks. You’ll join a team building the infrastructure that makes these outcomes repeatable at scale. About the role As a Sales Lead at Scarlet you will lead a team of Account Executives in London, grow that team, as well as continue closing deals yourself. You will own your team's quarterly number and the pipeline behind it. Our sales team has grown fast and is about to grow faster so we'll need your help to continue to build the team and develop our talent. You will carry a personal quota alongside your team target, which will be reduced as your team grows, so you stay close to customers and lead from live deals rather than from a dashboard. The deals are technical: you are selling certification to regulatory, quality and clinical leaders at AI and software medical device companies, and you will need to build deep knowledge of EU MDR, ISO 13485 and other medical device certifications. Our best salespeople know the product in depth, and we expect the same of you. You will work day to day with our leadership team, Business Development Reps, Commercial Relations and Customer Experience. This is a full-time, in-office role in London where your team will also be located. Practice what you preach: source, run and close your own deals with regulatory, quality and clinical leaders at AI and software medical device companies. Share what works: write up deal learnings and losses for the wider sales team, and bring improvements to the playbook, qualification and pricing conversations. Work with the BDR team on first-meeting-to-discovery conversion and with Commercial Relations on partner and consultant referrals. Represent Scarlet with your team at industry conferences (for example MEDICA, RSNA) and at Scarlet-hosted events. Required qualifications 5+ years of B2B sales experience, including at least 3 years as a quota-carrying Account Executive owning full-cycle deals At least 1 year managing or formally leading quota-carrying salespeople, with responsibility for their targets A track record of hitting or exceeding quota as an individual contributor, including in the year before you moved into management Experience hiring salespeople: screening, interviewing and making hiring decisions Experience selling a technical or expertise-led product to specialist buyers, with deal cycles of three months or more and multiple stakeholders Experience running pipeline reviews and forecasting a team or territory number to senior leadership Able to show how you have coached an underperforming AE back to target, with the evidence you used Based in, or willing to relocate to, London, with the right to work in the UK Preferred qualifications A STEM degree or equivalent technical background Experience in selling to regulated industries Experience as an early sales hire or first sales manager at a startup, where you helped build the process rather than inherit it Experience selling into European markets outside the UK Compensation and benefits The base salary range for this role is £100,000 – £120,000 per year, with on-target earnings of £200,000 – £240,000. title: Founding Growth Associate
description: Odin is building the investment infrastructure for the future of private markets. We believe capital is one of the most powerful tools for shaping the world - and more people should know how to put it to work. Our mission is to make it radically easier to raise and deploy capital, so that anyone, anywhere, can back the companies and ideas they believe in. Our first product is a full-stack platform for launching and running private investment firms, allowing you to run everything from your phone - think Shopify for VC and PE. We handle all the infrastructure: from legal structuring and investor onboarding to KYC/AML, payments, tax, reporting, and exits. We're already trusted by over 10,000 angels, VCs, and founders. We administer over $750m in assets, covering investments from pre-seed to series E. This includes household names like ElevenLabs, OpenAI, SpaceX, xAI, Anduril, etc. but also new companies creating everything from synthetic brains to small nuclear reactors. Why we're hiring We're past product-market fit and growing 2x year on year, almost entirely through word of mouth, Google and AI search. Around 70 new leads land each month without a growth engine behind them, and you'll play a pivotal role in building one alongside the founders. Our co-founder Paddy is taking direct ownership of growth, and he wants a commercially minded builder alongside him: someone who'd rather make the thing than talk about it. You'll sit in the founders' office, working directly with Paddy on whatever moves the number most, from partnerships and events to building something that brings in 50 qualified leads in a month. The goal is 7,000 deals a year. Getting there depends on more of the right people finding us. What you'll build You'll work directly with Paddy , our co-founder, with the freedom to try things fast and the backing to scale what works Growth mechanisms: Lead magnets, micro products, tools and campaigns that bring syndicate leads and fund managers to Odin. You build the actual thing with AI, not a strategy deck about it. Think a calculator every new fund manager bookmarks, or a tool that turns a syndicate lead's first deal into a week's work instead of a month's. Ship it, see what works, double down. Partnerships: Co-investors, syndicate networks, accelerators and fund admins already talk to the people we want to reach. You find the ones who can send us the right people and get them live. Events: Pitch nights, GP-LP mixers and founder dinners for a community that backs everything from AI labs to small nuclear reactors. You'll turn that into new customers. Referrals and repeat: Our existing customers already come back again and again. You'll build the ways they bring others with them. Special projects: The founders' office gets the problems that matter and don't have an owner yet. You'll pick them up, work out what's true and get them done. What we're looking for Exceptionally sharp: At least a couple of years in a role that's trained you to think fast and rigorously. That might be consulting, banking, VC, a founder associate or chief of staff role, or early-stage growth. A commercially minded builder: You love making things, and you think about who they're for and whether they'll move the number before you start. You build with AI: You ship things yourself rather than waiting for someone else to execute your ideas, and you can show us what you've made. Analytical and financially literate: You're comfortable with numbers, you can tell what's working from the data, and you understand how capital moves. Taste and creative flair: You know what will land with a sophisticated audience of investors and founders, and what won't. Fast-moving and self-directed: You make decisions without constant validation and you'd rather ship something today than perfect it next month. Outcomes over activity: Pipeline and revenue are what you optimise for, not impressions or output volume. Credible with investors: Comfortable on a call with a seasoned GP or in a room full of them. Big plus: private markets exposure: VC, angel syndicates or fund admin. Useful, but not required. How we work There are five things we care about deeply: Reason from the ground up: Seek to understand what is true by always asking why. Do not trust convention or experts. Speed begets speed: We work fast. Speed compounds, it's the best form of defensibility, and it's energising to be around. If you work slowly, or tolerate slow work around you, you do not belong at Odin. Take ownership: Do not wait for permission to do things. Find the answer, force the thing into existence and hold others to an extremely high standard - the same standard you hold yourself to. Brutal honesty: If work doesn't meet the bar, people need to hear it, and the right people want to. This role is probably not for you if You want a well-defined lane and a fully built playbook; You'd rather write the strategy than build and ship the thing yourself; You need a team underneath you to get things done; Salary £60,000–£70,000 base, plus bonus and a meaningful equity grant. Hiring process Four stages: an intro call with Imani , our Head of People, a call with Paddy, a 90-minute build task, and a final with our founders. Detailed feedback within 24 hours of each one. Location & ways of working We're a London-based team. This role works side by side with the founders, and the speed we run at makes that much easier in person. At least three days a week in the office. Benefits Health: Private health insurance (Vitality), paid sick leave including support for pregnancy loss and fertility treatments Parental Leave: Enhanced maternity, adoption, paternity and partner leave Pension: 4% employer contribution with salary sacrifice options Time Off: 25 days annual leave, 2 wellness days and flexible bank holidays (33 days total) Work From Anywhere: Up to 6 weeks per year working from anywhere globally Birthday Leave: An additional day of leave Compensation: £60K – £70K • Offers Equity • Offers Bonus • £60K – £70K • Offers Equity • Offers Bonus Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Technical Programme Manager
description: About us EggAI is a fast-growing AI consulting and development startup. We build agentic AI solutions for enterprise clients. We are growing in several European markets. The role You will lead our clients through the organisational and operational changes needed to establish a shared AI platform. The platform has two parts: an AI Control Plane that governs what agents may do and records the evidence, and a managed AI Runtime where the agents run. Both integrate with the client's identity, security, delivery and audit services, and both need owners, approval routes and support arrangements on the client side. You will own delivery outcomes from mobilisation through production release and operating handover, acting as the client sponsor's day-to-day counterpart. The role reaches across engineering, business leadership, security, risk, compliance and operations. You will bring these groups together to agree how the platform is governed and supported, and what evidence they need for assurance in a regulated environment. You will lead an EggAI delivery team with a mix of Platform Engineering roles and skills. Client application teams develop the business use cases; you lead AI platform delivery and the changes needed for teams to adopt and operate it. Why this role Most organisations are still working out how to let AI agents act safely in production: who approves what an agent may do, how its actions are evidenced, and who answers when something goes wrong. There is no settled playbook yet, especially in regulated industries. In this role you will help write it. The operating models, approval routes and assurance practices you design with our clients will shape how they run agentic AI for years, and they will become the basis of how EggAI delivers across Europe. You will work at the point where AI capability meets enterprise reality, with direct access to client sponsors and EggAI leadership, and with real influence over how a growing company builds its delivery practice. Responsibilities - Own the delivery plan and milestones, keeping commitments achievable within the agreed scope, budget and team capacity. - Secure the client commitments that delivery depends on. Agree who will provide access, complete service changes and make decisions, then resolve delays with the responsible teams. - Design the target operating model with the client. Define who owns the platform service, maintains policies and software, supports the runtime and approves changes, with agreed escalation routes. - Run milestone acceptance. Submit evidence for each milestone, secure recorded client decisions within agreed review periods and escalate overdue or disputed decisions. - Lead change control with the sponsor and EggAI leadership. Agree scope, capacity, cost and date changes, including proposals for additional services or extended support, before committing the team. - Secure production readiness. Confirm the service owners and funded operating cover from the operating model are in place before go-live, escalating any gap that prevents release. - Lead go-live coordination and the intensive support period after release. Bring client operations and application teams together to resolve incidents and agree when normal support can take over. - Lead platform adoption and training with the technical team, preparing client teams to use shared controls and follow the agreed delivery processes. - Run operating handover through practical exercises. Secure acceptance of ongoing duties and agree any further support needed before the current engagement ends. - Give sponsors a clear account of progress and delivery risks through weekly delivery reviews, regular demonstrations and sponsor reviews. Report spending, forecast work and adoption results so they can make timely decisions. What You Bring - You have led technology programmes into production in a regulated environment, including operational readiness and handover to receiving teams. - You have designed and introduced operating models, turning agreed responsibilities into working approval, support and service-management processes. - You have led delivery across engineering teams, client departments and external partners, including influencing senior sponsors and resolving competing priorities. - You have managed budgets and contractual scope in client delivery, including negotiating changes and shaping additional work. - You understand cloud platforms, security and service operations well enough to challenge plans and dependencies with technical specialists. - You communicate clearly and can lead workshops that turn disagreement or uncertainty into decisions and action. Nice to have Delivery in financial services or banking. AI platforms or agentic AI. Platform engineering, identity, security controls or audit and assurance work. Cloud platform delivery using Azure (preferred), AWS or Google Cloud, and AI platform services such as Microsoft Foundry. German is a strong advantage, as many of our clients are in the DACH region. Practical details - Hybrid working and client-site attendance will depend on the engagement. - You will need to complete the background and security checks required by the client. We'd love to hear from you! If your profile looks like a good match we'll be in touch to organise a first stage interview. Please note, due to the high volume of candidates, we cannot offer personalized feedback to each candidate. Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

As well as <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/personal">personal</a> and <a href="https://monzo.com/business-banking">business</a> bank accounts, we offer <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/joint-account">joint accounts</a>, <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/16-17">accounts for 16-17 year olds</a>, a <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/under-16s">free kids account</a> and <a href="https://monzo.com/flex">credit cards</a> in the UK, with more exciting things to come beyond. Our UK customers can also <a href="https://monzo.com/savings">save</a>, <a href="https://monzo.com/investments">invest </a>and <a href="https://monzo.com/pensions">combine their pensions</a> with us. </p> <p>With our hot coral cards and get-paid-early feature, combined with financial education on social media and our award winning customer service, we have a long history of creating magical moments for our customers!</p> <p>We’re not about selling products - we want to solve problems and change lives through Monzo ❤️</p> <hr> <p> </p></div><p>📍London | 💰£67,000 Total OTE (base salary + commission) <a href="https://monzo.com/careers/">Benefits</a> | <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U62l09nB0M4">Hear from the team</a> ✨<strong><br><br></strong></p> <p><strong>⭐ About our Business Banking Sales team</strong></p> <p>We are rapidly growing and now serve over 730,000 businesses in the UK 🇬🇧</p> <p>In order to support the next phase of our expansion, we’re hiring a small team of experienced <strong>Sales Account Executives</strong>, whose mission is to reach out and support more complex high value customers with a personalised experience. </p> <p>We’re building an acquisition engine and your job will be to work with small-medium business (SMB) prospective customers, guide them through their buying journey, work with them to activate their account and bring all their banking needs to Monzo. </p> <p>This is an exciting opportunity to be a part of the founding sales team for a mission driven company , which is changing how people and businesses bank. </p> <p><strong>🔑 You’ll play a key role by…</strong></p> <ul> <li>Engaging with prospective SMB customers through discovery calls, and understand their business, challenges, goals and requirements.</li> <li>Driving full sales cycle, from early prospecting and qualification; to demos and sales;  to ensuring successful account switch and activation.</li> <li>Guiding customers through Monzo’s business banking offerings - providing clear, factual information and helping them evaluate what works best.</li> <li>Being a product expert: fully understand Monzo's business banking products, features and services.</li> <li>Managing a pipeline of leads with strong attention to data hygiene: timely follow-ups, accurate forecasting, deal tracking.</li> <li>Driving activation: not just closing, but ensuring new business customers are fully set up, onboarded, and are using Monzo for their banking needs.</li> <li>Collaborating internally: work closely with marketing, product, risk and customer operations to ensure a smooth journey for customers.</li> <li>Delivering outstanding service at every touchpoint: via phone, video, email or digital channels.</li> <li>Achieving sales targets: conversion, activations, revenue, engagement and other growth metrics as set by the commercial leadership.</li> <li>Feeding insights back: capture and share customer feedback — customer pain points, required features, suggestions for product improvements.</li> <li>Adapting & iterate: Things will change rapidly and often - you’ll need to be comfortable with ambiguity and change and help support what comes next.</li> </ul> <p><strong>🤩 We’d love to hear from you if you...</strong></p> <ul> <li>Have experience in Small Business sales, ideally selling business solutions or financial services; knowing how to engage business customers and understand their mindset, needs and pain points.</li> <li>Have a proven track record of meeting (or exceeding) sales quotas / targets in a performance-driven environment.</li> <li>Are an expert at managing a full sales cycle: from prospecting to activation, including structured and rigorous outreach and follow-ups and cross-team coordination.</li> <li>Have high emotional intelligence and are able to quickly connect and build a relationship with customers of diverse backgrounds and levels of knowledge.</li> <li>Are a strategic communicator,  excellent at building trust and helping customers discover value - you’re consultative, you listen, you ask insightful questions.</li> <li>Are adaptable and resilient, you embrace change and have a strong winning mindset to see challenges as opportunities to learn and grow.</li> <li>Can communicate clearly: written, verbal, via video; you simplify complex topics for customers.</li> <li>Are coachable and comfortable seeking constructive criticism to empower continuous learning and improvement</li> <li>Are comfortable working in a fast-moving, high change environment. You thrive when things aren’t fully defined yet.</li> <li>Can demonstrate high levels of personal organisation: tracking your pipeline, managing your time, prioritising your leads and follow-up tasks.</li> <li>Have integrity and strong consumer duty awareness: regulatory compliance, knowing your customer, reducing risk, safeguarding data and ensuring we put consumer duty first are foundational to this role and our culture.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Bonus / Nice-to-haves:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Prior experience in a regulated environment (banking)</li> <li>Experience with Salesforce</li> <li>Familiarity with SMBs in specific verticals (e.g. food & drink, professional services, construction)</li> </ul> <p><strong>🙌 What’s in it for you</strong></p> <p>💰 £67,000 Total OTE (base salary + commission)</p> <p>📍 4 days a week in our London office but with occasional flexibility to work remotely (in the UK)</p> <p>⏰ We offer flexible working hours and trust you to work enough hours to do your job well, and at times that suit you and your team. </p> <p>📚 £1,000 learning budget each year to use on books, training courses and conferences.</p> <p>🏡 We will set you up to work from home; all employees are given Macbooks and for fully remote workers we will provide extra support for your work-from-home setup. </p> <p>➕ Plus lots more! <a href="https://monzo.com/careers/">Read our full list of benefits</a>.</p> <p><strong>🌈 The application journey has the following key steps</strong></p> <ul> <li>Phone call with recruiter (30 mins)</li> <li>Sales experience video interview with Sales Lead (45 mins)</li> <li>In-person assessment: Practical task assessment + Team and Culture fit interview (90 mins)</li> </ul> <p>This process should take around 4-6 weeks - your schedule is really important to us, so we promise to be as flexible as possible! </p> <p>We have some guidelines on using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to ace an application and interview at Monzo 🤖 <a href="https://monzo.com/blog/the-ultimate-guide-on-using-ai-to-ace-an-interview-at-monzo">You can read them here.</a></p> <p>#LI-NZ1</p><div class="content-conclusion"><hr> <p><strong>Equal opportunities for everyone</strong></p> <p>Diversity and inclusion are a priority for us and we’re making sure we have lots of support for all of our people to grow at Monzo. At Monzo, we’re embracing diversity by fostering an inclusive environment for all people to do the best work of their lives with us. This is integral to our mission of making money work for everyone. You can read more in our <a href="https://monzo.com/blog/diversity-and-inclusion">blog</a>, 2026 <a href="https://monzo.com/blog/our-2026-diversity-and-inclusion-report" target="_blank">Diversity and Inclusion Report</a> and 2025 <a href="https://monzo.com/blog/gender-pay-gap-report-2025">Gender Pay Gap Report.</a></p> <p>We’re an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to age, ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, or veteran, neurodiversity or disability status.</p> <p>If you have a preferred name, please use it to apply. We don't need full or birth names at application stage 😊</p></div>

title: Business Recruiter
